newsitem.title: USA: Sunamerica to buy John Alden annuity business.
newsitem.headline: Sunamerica to buy John Alden annuity business.

text.p: SunAmerica Inc.'s wholly owned subsidiary, SunAmerica Life Insurance Co., has agreed to acquire the annuity business of John Alden Financial Corp. for about $240 million in cash, the companies said Monday.
The sale is part of Miami-based John Alden's plan to focus on its health insurance business.

With the purchase, SunAmerica would have about $42 billion of assets, including $29 billion on its balance sheet, more than $2 billion managed in mutual funds and private accounts, and $11 billion under custody in retirement trust accounts.
The deal includes about $5.0 billion of annuity reserves, including about $3.7 billion of reserves from John Alden Life Insurance Co. under a reinsurance contract.
SunAmerica will also buy John Alden Life Insurance Co. of New York, which had about $1.3 billion of annuity reserves and $71 million of adjusted capital and surplus as of Sept. 30.
"This transaction is in keeping with SunAmerica's strategy to enhance our dynamic internal growth with complementary acquisitions," said Eli Broad, chairman and chief executive officer of SunAmerica.
"This acquisition will increase our annuity reserves from $16 billion to $21 billion, giving us greater critical mass and lowering our unit operating costs."
Los Angeles-based SunAmerica said it expects the deal to boost earnings immediately.
"We made a decision earlier this year to focus the company's resources exclusively on our healthcare lines," said John Alden Chairman Glendon E. Johnson.

John Alden said it expects to post a net deferred gain of about $45 million from the sale and the company's previously announced intention to sell its credit operations. The net deferred gain will be recognised as income as SunAmerica completes the assumption of policyholder liabilities, it said.
Alden said it expects to begin recognising the gain in 1997 and to earn the majority of the gain in 1998.
It also said its available capital will be enhanced by both the after-tax income generated from the sale and the release of the capital previously allocated to support the annuity business.

Alden said it plans to use part of this capital to strengthen its healthcare operations, after which an estimated $175 million to $200 million will be available mainly to buy back common stock, pay down debt and for general corporate purposes.
The transaction includes about 250,000 policies, a major portion of which are subject to surrender charges, making the block of business highly persistent, SunAmerica said.

Most of the assets are high-quality, liquid investments, virtually all of which are rated investment grade. They also include a well-underwritten, seasoned portfolio of commercial and residential mortgage loans, SunAmerica said.
The deal is expected to close by March 1997, subject to regulatory approvals, the companies said.
SunAmerica stock fell 50 cents to $41.375 and John Alden lost 37.5 cents to $17.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
